pr_title: planner: steady expression index selection when having duplicate expressions
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #25729 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

- expressional index can be used when have duplicate expression

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

- Change the logic in selectivity computation in `selectivity.go`.
- Change the logic in virtual column comparison.

How it Works:

- When we have expression indexes that have duplicate expressions, we will have duplicate generated virtual columns. They are one-to-one mapping. Previously, we substitute the expression in the logical plan with a random one of the duplicate generated virtual columns. This will make other duplicate virtual columns pruned out in the logical optimization process. Eventually, a random expression index will be selected. 

- After this commit, we will not prune out the duplicate virtual columns, and let all the expression index paths go into the physical optimization process. Therefore, an optimal index will be selected.

- The selectivity computation of `datasource` will also consider expression indexes that have duplicate expressions after this commit.

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

Side effects

- Some execution plans might change.
- Code complexity.

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- planner: steady expression index selection when having duplicate expressions
